title: PolyyAI can make 3D models and 2D aware sprites. We are planning to publicly launch later this Fall!
author: Polyy-AI

comments.author: Polyy-AI
comments.body: I've been working on AI workflows and game experiments for years, and am currently developing [Polyy.AI](https://polyy.ai/?ref=reddit_ai_game_dev_9-8-2026) which can make 3D assets and 2D assets that are 3D aware. I am planning to launch GA later this Fall. Outside of this I am a professional software engineer and pretty chill person so open to hearing any constructive feedback

comments.author: Significant_Tell407
comments.body: What do you mean when you say a 2D sprite is 3D aware? Are you saying it generates the sprite from every angle 360 degrees around the 2D object? Could definitely be valuable with rise of the 2.5D aesthetic in games

replies.author: Polyy-AI
replies.body: It generates a sprite from every angle, and it also provides normal mapping. We have a lot of free assets on itch, but [here](https://polyyai.itch.io/city-builder-commercial-buildings-73-pack) is an example that shows it pretty well, the sprites are easy to use in shaders because of the normal maps

replies.author: Significant_Tell407
replies.body: Amazing I cant wait to test it!

comments.author: Reasonable-Road-2279
comments.body: Good, but it have to be cheaper than hiring an actual human artist else what's the point. What is your pricing?

replies.author: Polyy-AI
replies.body:
It will be a lot cheaper than anything else on the market for full 3D assets that we can find in this quality! 

We haven't fully determined pricing points to protect us from cloud overspend, but at the moment it's looking like you'd be able to generate all 25 of the assets you see here, along with free infinite 3D aware sprite generation in as many palettes and resolutions and angles as you'd like, for ~$3.50-$4.00

On Tripo the same assets would cost $20-$25 (although their model is frontier, but ours can handle many of the same cases just fine)

comments.author: seahorse-emoji
comments.body: Looks impressive, the art style on the site and here seems fairly similar, I'm curious how well can you direct it to make different styles ?

replies.author: Polyy-AI
replies.body: I tend to use a lot of the same palettes for examples, but it is great at a wide variety of styles in both 3D and 2D. [Here](https://polyyai.itch.io/polyy-mossy-forest) is an example of something that wasn't output with the same yliluoma dithering and palette

replies.body: we understand! The model generation approach is more novel and difficult to replicate especially for our cost. The pixelization is just a cool rendering pipeline that is free for users to use and happens in-browser

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body: You can do the same thing with free tools. Just use a free 3D model generator, then load it into Blender and render it using one of the many free pixel render addons.

replies.author: Polyy-AI
replies.body: what "free 3D model generator" would you use? Ours requires a lot of cloud GPU so it's not really consumer hardware ready. Our pixel rendering pipeline from the model gen is free.

replies.author: ThatzBudiz
replies.body: there arent any short of 2 or 3 free models with no download short of running hunyuan locally (or the 20 they give per day)

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
There's free options if someone has the hardware. 

You're really just competing with all the other 3D model gen services because the pixel rendering part is the easiest part of the process. So you're going to need to be either a lot better or a lot cheaper than services like Meshy and Tripo etc. 

Unless you've trained your own model which is highly doubtful then you've also probably just made a wrapper for an existing open source model anyway.

replies.author: Polyy-AI
replies.body:
We have custom modified Trellis 2 to be capable of open-source compatible generations which it is not by default because it uses several proprietary licensing dependencies, and we have also retrained and tuned the model on top of that.

Additionally like I have said in this thread, it's a lot cheaper than Tripo and Meshy per model
